title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 318-319 of the 'Longue Marche' sequel). An automorphism u of the profinite free group Π̂_{0,3} = <l_0, l_1, l_∞ | l_0 l_1 l_∞ = 1> is given in 'Galois/GT form' by (11): u(l_0) = int(g_0)(l_0^χ), and similar formulas for l_1 and l_∞. Here χ ∈ Ẑ* is the 'cyclotomic' exponent; the image writes it as a small p/ρ-like superscript, distinct from the order-3 element ρ. Grothendieck transports u to the profinite completion Ĝ^+_{0,3} of the group generated by σ_∞ (order 2) and ρ (order 3). This is the modular group PSL_2(Z)^ = (Z/2 * Z/3)^, the orbifold fundamental group of the j-line / M_{1,1}. The comparison map (next page, (18)) is φ̂: l_0 ↦ σ_∞ρ = ε_0 (the parabolic/cusp element), l_1 ↦ σ_∞, l_∞ ↦ ρ^{-1}. By (15) the transported action is u(σ_∞) = σ_∞ and u(ρ) = gρ, with g = σ_∞(g_0) l_1^γ ρ(g_0)^{-1} (ρ(x) meaning ρxρ^{-1}).

This page checks that the defining relations of Z/2*Z/3 are respected.
- u(σ_∞)^2 = 1 is trivial.
- u(ρ)^3 = (gρ)^3 = g·ρ(g)·ρ^2(g)·ρ^3, so u(ρ)^3 = 1 reduces to the cocycle condition (16): g ρ(g) ρ^2(g) = 1. He says this follows from the explicit form (15) of g together with relation (10), presumably the 3-cycle ('hexagon') relation on g_0.

He then notes the expected cusp condition (17): u(l'_0) = int(g_0)(l'_0^χ), where l'_0 = σ_∞ρ = ε_0. The image's parenthesis appears to be '(donc l'_0^2 = l_0)', i.e. l_0 ↦ ε_0^2 under the index-6 inclusion Π_{0,3} ≅ Γ(2) ⊂ PSL_2(Z), where the cusp at λ = 0 has ramification 2 over j = ∞. Then (17) would be the 'square root' of (11): u(l'_0)^2 = int(g_0)(l'_0^{2χ}). His bracketed remark is that (17) does follow, provided one knows that the centralizer of the cusp group L_0 = l_0^Ẑ is L_0 itself (uniqueness of the square root).

Finally he expects the torsion conditions (18): u(ρ) should be conjugate to ρ^χ. The image says 'conjugués dans Π̂_{0,3}', presumably meaning Ĝ. He states it is not clear to him whether these follow from the conditions imposed so far, and promises to return to them.

Purpose: build the action of a GT/Galois-type element on π̂_1^orb(M_{1,1}) = PSL_2(Z)^ compatibly with its action on π̂_{0,3}, i.e. the passage from genus 0 to genus 1 in the Teichmüller tower.
errors: The cusp element l'_0 = ε_0 lies in Ĝ, not in Π̂_{0,3}. To extract a square root one needs the centralizer of the cusp subgroup inside Ĝ = (Z/2*Z/3)^, not inside Π̂_{0,3] as written. The step is fine but the stated hypothesis is placed in the wrong group.
Relation (18) is written as 'conjugate in Π̂_{0,3}'. Since ρ ∉ Π̂_{0,3}, this must mean conjugacy in Ĝ^+_{0,3}.
There is notational ambiguity between the order-3 generator ρ and the cyclotomic exponent (written p/ρ). The transcription conflates them; the exponent is presumably χ(σ) ∈ Ẑ*.

ideas.what: Action of a GT/Galois-type automorphism on PSL_2(Z)^ = (Z/2*Z/3)^ by σ_∞ ↦ σ_∞, ρ ↦ gρ, transported from π̂_{0,3} via the j-line orbifold map
ideas.modern_name: Action of GT on the profinite modular group / B_3^ / Γ̂_{1,1}
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions genus 1 / modular group in the Teichmüller tower; details in La Longue Marche (circulated)

ideas.what: Reduction of u(ρ)^3 = 1 to the cocycle condition g ρ(g) ρ^2(g) = 1, deduced from the 3-cycle relation
Deducing the cusp condition for ε_0 from the one for l_0 = ε_0^2 via self-centralizing cusp subgroups
ideas.modern_name: Self-centralizing (malnormal) inertia/cusp subgroups in profinite surface groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Nakamura; Herfort–Ribes (centralizers in profinite free products)

ideas.what: Expected condition that torsion generators go to conjugates of their χ-powers (u(ρ) ~ ρ^χ)
ideas.modern_name: Inertia-preservation for torsion/orbifold points; branch-cycle condition in genus 1
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps; Herfort–Ribes theorem on torsion in free profinite products

missed.claim: Grothendieck leaves open whether the torsion-conjugacy conditions (18) follow from the GT-type conditions (9)-(11). Herfort–Ribes (profinite Kurosh/torsion theorem) shows any order-3 element of (Z/2*Z/3)^ is conjugate to ρ^{±1}, and abelianization fixes the sign. So this is a gap later closed by known results rather than a new open problem.
missed.quote: il n'est pas clair pour moi qu'elles soit conséquences des conditions envisagées jusqu'à présent
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historically documents that Grothendieck isolated the genus-1 torsion/inertia conditions later studied in Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps-type refinements of GT. Mathematically it appears resolved.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but standard verification that the GT-type action on π̂_{0,3} descends to the profinite modular group (hexagon ⇔ order-3 cocycle), now well known from Drinfeld/Ihara/Lochak–Schneps. The open question about torsion conjugacy is answered by known profinite free-product theory. Only modest historical interest as an early isolation of genus-1 inertia conditions.
transcription_corrections: Exponents written 'ρ' in (11) and (17) (e.g. l_0^ρ, l_0'^p) are the cyclotomic exponent (χ), not the order-3 element ρ.
'(donc ℓ_0'^2 = ℓ_0 [?])' appears to read '(d'où l'_0^2 = l_0)', i.e. l_0 is the square of the cusp element under the index-6 embedding.
In (18), '=' is struck and replaced by 'conjugués dans', with 'mod' struck; the group written is Π̂_{0,3} with a hat (likely meaning Ĝ).
